objective: Define the authority boundary that must be satisfied after patched Verilator native option parse success and before any native-invocation sidecar build, run, compare, timing, arbitrary RTL/filelist support, automatic GPU allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw full-state equality, or production LLM-serving throughput claim.

definition_decision.weakest_point: Parser-only success plus generated patched binary evidence is not sidecar execution authority.

failure_class_boundary.process_parse_failure: Verilator process does not accept the native option spelling or setup fails before sidecar authority.
failure_class_boundary.sidecar_authority_failure: Parser success exists but explicit sidecar context, artifact provenance, reviewed stage authority, or compare policy is incomplete.
failure_class_boundary.sidecar_stage_failure: Reviewed authority exists but build or run stage fails.
failure_class_boundary.compare_failure: Build/run completes but the declared compare policy fails.
failure_class_boundary.timing_claim_without_measurement: A command includes parser/build timing input or runtime logs without an accepted timing measurement gate.

defined_next_run_prerequisites: start from the reviewed parser-only patched-binary success gate
use a reviewed patched binary artifact or record an equivalent rebuild
keep VERILATOR_ROOT as mechanical process setup, not source of truth
validate explicit sidecar context before any sidecar handoff
use one reviewed target/template and shape for the first native-invocation sidecar execution run
record build, run, and compare as separate stage evidence
compare only named coverage-output words under coverage_output_equivalence
keep timing, speedup, arbitrary filelist inference, automatic GPU allocation, runtime/ABI change, and raw full-state equality out of scope unless a later gate defines them

required_next_gate.name: review_verilator_native_option_parser_direct_command_path_native_invocation_sidecar_authority_boundary_gate
must_decide: whether parser-only success plus this authority definition is sufficient to prepare a first scoped sidecar execution run
whether artifact provenance remains non-canonical enough for a future execution boundary
whether explicit sidecar context and reviewed stage authority are complete enough
whether compare-output words and coverage_output_equivalence are sufficiently separated from raw full-state equality
whether all timing, speedup, arbitrary RTL/filelist, automatic allocation, runtime/ABI, raw-state, and production throughput claims remain out of scope

non_claims: not broad native Verilator option support
not source-closure or filelist dependency inference
not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
